He will be the arranger of the Vedas, the maker of the Kuru line, and the author of the Itihasa, your son, for the good of the world.
mahabharata:13:18.31	That great sage, Parashara's son, will be dear to Mahendra, ageless and deathless.
Having so spoken, the blessed one vanished right there, Yudhishthira, the great yogi, mighty, unwounded and imperishable.
[Mandavya said:] "When I, innocent, was impaled on a stake on suspicion of theft, praised by me there, the god Maheshvara said to me:
'You will be freed from the stake and live a hundred million years; no pain from the stake will be yours, Brahmana; you will be free of mental and bodily sicknesses.
Since your self was born from a quarter of my foot, sage, you will be incomparable; make your birth fruitful.
Your bathing at sacred fords will be fruitful, and without obstacle you will gain imperishable heaven, Brahmana; I ordain that for you.'
Having so spoken, the blessed one, the choicest, bull-rider, Maheshvara, great king, clad in a hide, of great splendour, with his host, best of the gods, vanished right there."
[Galava said:] "Permitted by Vishvamitra, I came to my father; then my mother, sorrowful and weeping greatly, said to me:
'A son permitted by Kaushika and adorned with the Veda, dear one, your father does not see you young and self-controlled, sinless one.'
Hearing my mother's word, hopeless of seeing my teacher, I restrained myself and saw Mahadeva, and he said to me:
'You, your father and mother, son, will be free of death; enter quickly; you will see your father at home.'
Permitted by the blessed one, I went home, Yudhishthira, and saw my father, dear one, coming out after performing a sacrifice.
Having touched water and taken fuel and kusha grass, from the shelter, and dismissing those elders, my father said to me, his eyes full of tears:
'Embracing me as I bowed, smelling my head, Pandava: By good fortune you are seen by me, son, having come here with your learning done.'"
[Vaishampayana said:] Hearing those very wonderful deeds of the great soul told by the sages, the Pandava was astonished.
Then Krishna, best of the wise, spoke again to Yudhishthira, ever devoted to dharma, like the lord to Purahuta:

The sun and moon, wind and fire, heaven, earth, waters, the Vasus and Vishvedevas, Dhatri, Aryaman, Shukra and Brihaspati, the Rudras with the Sadhyas, Varuna, the guardian of wealth,
mahabharata:13:18.48	Brahma, Shakra, the Maruts, Brahman and truth, the Vedas, sacrifices, fee, the carriers of the Vedas, Soma the sacrificer, whatever is the offering and oblation, protection, initiation and observances,
mahabharata:13:18.49	svaha and vashat, brahmanas, cows, dharma, the wheel, the wheel of time, the moving, fame, self-control, understanding and steadiness, the good and the bad, and the seven sages,
mahabharata:13:18.50	foremost understanding, with the mind in seeing, success in touch, and the success of deeds, the hosts of gods, the heat-drinkers and Soma-drinkers, the Lekhas, Suyamas, Tushitas and Brahmakayas,
mahabharata:13:18.51	the Abhasvaras, smell-drinkers and sight-drinkers, those opposed in speech and in mind, the pure, gods delighting in extinction, touch-eaters, new-moon-drinkers and ghee-drinkers,
mahabharata:13:18.52	those who have gone to thought, who are chief among the gods, and the other deities, Ajamidha, the suparnas, gandharvas, pishachas, danavas, yakshas, nagas and charanas,
mahabharata:13:18.53	the subtle and the gross, the soft and the non-subtle, pleasure and pain and what lies between pleasure and pain, Sankhya and yoga and what is beyond breaths: know that this is born of Sharva, as I have said.
mahabharata:13:18.54	Born from him are the makers of beings, the choicest, all the gods who are guardians of this world, who entering this earth protected the ancient creation of that god.
mahabharata:13:18.55	I praise him who is searched for in mind; I bow for the sake of some truth, for life; may that god give the wished boons here, the unchanging lord, praised by us always.
Restraining his senses, becoming pure, the man who recites this hymn with unbroken yoga and restraint for a year gains the fruit of the horse sacrifice.
A brahmana would gain all the Vedas; a king would conquer the whole earth; a vaishya would gain profit and skill; a shudra would gain a goal after death and happiness.
Having made this king of hymns, they set their minds on Rudra, a holy, purifying and glorious one that removes all faults.
As many pores of hair as are on his body, Bharata, so many thousand years does the man dwell in heaven.
[Yudhishthira said:] Whether this dharma be that of the sages, of Prajapati or of the asuras, what was said before by great sages, "the joint dharma",
this is a very great doubt, and I think it is contradictory. Where is this joint dharma ordained after death?
Among the dead in heaven there is joint dharma, grandfather; but one dies first, and where does the other remain? Tell me.
Possessed of the fruits of various deeds, living in various works, with various hells as their end, when men are many,
the author of the aphorisms rules "women are untrue"; when women are untrue, dear one, how is joint dharma remembered?
Women are untrue: this is read even in the Vedas; this dharma is an old name, a courtesy, a rule of rite.
This seems a deep matter as I think of it day and night; all this without doubt, grandfather, as scripture says.
What it is, of what kind, and how it has been set going, you ought to tell me in full, greatly wise one.
[Bhishma said:] Long ago Ashtavakra, of great austerity, wishing to marry, asked for the daughter of a bountiful great-souled sage.
Named Suprabha, incomparable in beauty on earth, rich in qualities, virtuous in conduct, shining in behaviour.
The fair-eyed one took his mind at first sight, like a variegated forest row in spring covered with flowers.
The sage said to him, "My daughter is to be given to you; hear me: first go to the holy northern quarter; there you will see."
[Ashtavakra said:] "What shall I see there? You ought to tell me; I shall do what you tell me now."
[The sage said:] "Passing beyond the lord of wealth and the Himalaya, you will see Rudra's abode, frequented by Siddhas and Charanas,
served by delighted attendants dancing with various faces, with divine unguents, forest pishachas of many kinds,
with clapping, cymbals and measured beats, delighted ones dancing; there Sharva is attended.
We have heard that place on the mountain to be dear and divine; the god is ever near, and the auspicious attendants.
There the goddess practised very hard austerity for Shankara; therefore it is dear to the god and to Uma, so tradition says.
There is a great well on the side, north of the god, and the seasons and Kalaratri, divine and human,
all attend the god, embodied there. Passing that, you must go on to the dwelling.
Then you will see a blue forest region like a cloud; lovely and mind-seizing, there you will see a woman,
an ascetic, greatly fortunate, aged, following an initiation. She is to be seen and carefully honoured by you there.
Having seen her, turn back, and then you will take the hand; if this condition is true, let it be done; go there."
[Bhishma said:] Then the blessed one went to the best northern quarter, to the Himalaya, best of mountains, frequented by Siddhas and Charanas.
Going to the great mountain Himalaya, the tiger among the twice-born reached the holy river Bahuda, giver of dharma.
Bathing in the pure sacred ford of Ashoka and satisfying the gods, he happily lay there to stay on a bed of kusha grass.
Then, when the night had passed, rising in the morning, the brahmana bathed, lit the fire and offered by rule.
Reaching the Rudrani well there at the lake, he rested; refreshed he rose and went toward Kailasa.
He saw a golden gate shining with splendour, and the Mandakini and the lotus pond of the great-souled lord of wealth.
Then all the rakshasas who guard the lotus pond, headed by Manibhadra, rose to meet the blessed one.
He honoured those rakshasas of terrible prowess and said, "Quickly inform the lord of wealth of me."
Then Vaishravana came to the blameless Ashtavakra, asked him duly of his welfare and said to the Brahmarishi:

Have you come at ease? What do you wish from me? Say; I shall do all you tell me, twice-born.
mahabharata:13:20.14	Enter my house as you wish, best of the twice-born; honoured and with your task done, you will go without obstacle.
He took that best of the twice-born and entered his own house; he gave him his own seat, and foot-water and guest-water too.
Then as they sat there, the yakshas, gandharvas and rakshasas of Kubera, led by Manibhadra, sat.
Then as they sat, the lord of wealth said: "Knowing your wish, let the troops of apsarases dance.
Hospitality is the highest duty, and service to you." The sage said in a sweet voice, "Let it proceed."
Then Urvara, Mishrakeshi, Rambha and Urvashi, Alambusha, Ghritachi, Chitra, Chitrangada, Ruchi,
Manohara, Sukeshi, Sumukhi, Hasini, Prabha, Vidyuta, Prashama, Danta, Vidyota and Rati,
these and many other lovely apsarases danced, and the gandharvas played various instruments.
When the divine music went on, the sage stayed there, enjoying a divine year, of great austerity.
Then King Vaishravana said to the blessed one: "A full year has passed, Brahmana, while you watched here.
This domain, called Gandharva, is to be given up, Brahmana; let it go on as you wish, or as you say.
You are a guest to be honoured, and this is your house; let everything be commanded at once; we are subject to you."
Then the blessed one, pleased, answered Vaishravana: "I have been honoured as is fitting; I shall go, lord of wealth.
I am pleased, and all is suited to you, lord of wealth; by your grace, blessed one, and the great sage's, I shall go today on his command; be prosperous and wealthy."
Then the blessed one went out and set off facing north; he went by Kailasa, Mandara and Hema, all of them.
Passing those great mountains, the excellent place of the Kiratas, he circled it, bowing his head, restrained; descending to the ground, he became pure-souled then.
Having circled that mountain three times, he went north on level ground, led by joy.
Then he saw another lovely forest region, rich in roots and fruits of all seasons, and birds, adorned here and there with charming forest regions.
There the blessed one saw a divine hermitage, and mountains of various shapes made of gold and adorned with jewels, and lotus-ponds set in jewelled ground.
He saw many other very lovely things; the mind of that great sage of purified self delighted greatly.
There he saw a divine house of gold, wholly made of jewels, wonderful to look at, finer than the lord of wealth's house.
Where there were great palaces of various kinds like mountains, lovely celestial cars and various jewels,
the river Mandakini strewn with mandara flowers, self-luminous gems, and the ground adorned with diamonds.
With houses of many kinds, with gateways of varied jewels, covered with nets of pearls and adorned with gems, all around surrounded by lovely auspicious things that took the mind and eye.
The sage saw on every side delightful sights here and there; then a thought came to him: "Where shall my lodging be?"
Then going and standing at the door, he said: "Let those here know that a guest has come."
Then maidens came out of that house surrounded by others, seven maidens of many forms, lord, all charming.
Whichever maiden he saw, each took his mind; he could not hold it, and his mind sank.
Then steadiness arose in that wise brahmana. Then the maidens said to him, "Let the blessed one enter."
And of those of fine form and of that very house,
filled with curiosity, the brahmana entered the house. There he saw an old woman, free of dust, wearing garments, an aged woman seated on a couch, adorned with every ornament.
When he said, "Blessings," that woman replied, rose for that brahmana and said, "Be seated."
[Ashtavakra said:] "Let all go to their own houses; let one wait on me, well-informed and very calm; let the others go as they wish."
Then, circling that sage, the maidens went out of that house, but that old woman stayed.
Then, as he lay on the shining bed, she said to him, "Sleep also, good one, for the night is passing."
Thus spoken to by that brahmana in conversation, she lay down on a second bed, divine and bright.
Then, trembling in her limbs, giving cold as the pretext, she got onto the great sage's bed.
Welcome, welcome, said the blessed one to her; and she embraced the sage with her arms, with love, bull among men.
Seeing the sage unchanging, like a wooden wall, she was distressed and spoke with the sage:

Brahmana, women have no choice in desire; there is steadiness from a man. I am bewildered by desire; accept me who accept you.
mahabharata:13:20.54	Be glad, brahmana sage, come together with me; embrace me, Brahmana; I am greatly afflicted by desire for you.
mahabharata:13:20.55	This is the fruit of your austerity, righteous-souled one, that is honoured: sought by sight alone, accept me who accept you.
mahabharata:13:20.56	This house and this forest and whatever else you see: your lordship is everywhere, and in me, without doubt.
mahabharata:13:20.57	I shall do all desires; enjoy yourself with me in the lovely forest, Brahmana, which gives fruit of every desire.
mahabharata:13:20.58	I shall be in your power, and you will delight with me, enjoying all desires, divine and human.
mahabharata:13:20.59	There is nothing higher for women to do than union with a man; this is our highest fruit.
mahabharata:13:20.60	Women act on their own wish, impelled by desire, and are not burnt even going over very hot dust.
[Ashtavakra said:] "I shall never go to another's wife, good one; touching another's wife is condemned in the law books.
Know, good one, that I wish to marry; I swear by truth. I am ignorant of the objects of the senses; offspring is for dharma.
Thus I shall go to the worlds by sons, without doubt; know dharma, good one, and, knowing, desist."
[The woman said:] "Neither the wind, nor fire, nor Varuna, nor other gods are as dear to women, twice-born, as desire; women are devoted to pleasure.
One woman among a thousand is sometimes found here, and among a hundred thousand perhaps one is devoted to her husband.
These know neither father, nor family, nor mother, nor brothers, nor husband, nor sons, nor brothers-in-law.
Playing, they destroy families like the best rivers their banks; and Prajapati spoke of the faults of the slow in the slow."
[Bhishma said:] Then the sage, one-pointed, replied to that woman: "Sit as you please; say what you need."
That woman said: "Blessed one, you will see in due place and time; stay for now, greatly wise one; with your task done you will go."
The Brahmarishi said to her, "So be it," Yudhishthira; "I shall stay as long as you wish; there is no doubt."
Then the sage, looking at that woman afflicted with age, fell into great thought and was as if tormented.
Whatever limb of hers that bull among brahmanas saw, his eyes did not delight there, being overcome by the form.
This is the deity of this house, surely made ugly by a curse; it is not right for me to learn the cause of this suddenly.
While he was absorbed in thought, wishing to know the matter, the rest of that day passed with a troubled mind.
Then that woman said: "Blessed one, see the form of the sun joined with the evening cloud; what shall be set before you?"
He then said to her, "Bring water for bathing here; I shall perform twilight worship, silent and with senses restrained."
Permitted by the sage, that great soul, the woman then rubbed all his limbs with oil.
Gently rubbed, he went to the bathing room; then the sage entered a new, lovely high seat.
When he sat on that high seat, she bathed the sage slowly with a pleasant hand, and performed divine service duly for the sage.
By that very comfortable warmth and the pleasure of her hand, the great-vowed one did not know the whole night had passed.
Then the sage rose, greatly astonished, and saw the sun risen in the east in the sky.
His thought was: "What is this? Is this delusion or truth?" Then, having worshipped the thousand-rayed, he said to her, "What shall I do?"
She brought the sage food like the taste of nectar; from its sweetness he did not eat much, and the rest of the day passed, and evening came again.
Then the woman urged the blessed one, "Let us sleep," on a divine bed prepared there for him and her.
[The woman said:] "Desire for union torments me, Brahmana; see my devotion. You will incur unrighteousness, Brahmana, since you do not welcome me."
[Ashtavakra said:] "Faults born take a man as he wishes; I am always master by steadiness, good one; go to your own bed."
[The woman said:] "I bow my head, Brahmana; you ought to show favour; I fall on the ground; be my refuge, sinless one.
Or if you see a fault in other men's wives, I touch myself to you today; take my hand, twice-born.
There will be no fault; I say this by truth. Know me as independent; let whatever unrighteousness there is be on me."
[Ashtavakra said:] "How are you independent, good one? Tell me the reason; in the world no woman is fit for independence.
The father protects in childhood, the husband in youth, the sons in old age; a woman is not fit for independence."
[The woman said:] "My childhood is celibate; I am a maiden, without doubt. Do not hesitate, Brahmana; do not destroy my faith."
[Ashtavakra said:] "As it is for me, so for you; as it is for you, so for me; is this a test of the sage, or an obstacle to him? What is truth?
This is a supreme wonder; what is my good? This maiden, in divine ornaments and garments, has come to me.
How was her supreme form old, and how is it now a maiden's? What is the answer here?
As by the steadiness of the power of another I shall in no way rise up; I do not wish to rise up, and thus by steadiness I succeed."
[Bhishma said:] Ashtavakra asked her, "How do you change your form? And you must not tell me untruth, Brahmana, by your wish."
[The woman said:] "It is only of heaven and earth, best of brahmanas, this form I took on; hear all this with attention, truth-valiant one.
Know me as the northern quarter; you have seen woman's fickleness; by your not rising up, the worlds are conquered, truth-valiant one.
This test was applied by me to make you firm, sinless one; the fever of desire torments even aged women.
Your father is pleased today, and the gods with Vasava, and for what reason you, blessed one, came here.
I was sent by that brahmana, the maiden's father, bull among the twice-born, to teach you, and all that has been done by me.
You will go home safely and have no fatigue; you will gain that maiden, Brahmana, and have sons.
You asked me by your wish, and the answer has been given. This is not to be transgressed by all the three worlds ever.
I was propitiated by the sage for your sake, bull among the twice-born; to honour him I spoke this to you."
Hearing her word, the brahmana stood with joined palms and, permitted by her, returned to his own house.
Having reached home and rested, and honoured his own people, he duly went to that brahmana, delight of the Kurus.
Asked by that brahmana, "Was this illustration seen?", the brahmana, with a very pleased heart, told the brahmana.

Permitted by you I set out to Gandhamadana, and to the north of it in a place I saw that great deity.
mahabharata:13:22.16	And I was permitted by her, and you too were praised, and I have come home, lord, having made you hear that speech.
Then the brahmana said to him: "Accept my daughter; at the meeting of star and tithe, you are the best vessel."
[Bhishma said:] Saying "So be it," Ashtavakra, lord, accepted the maiden, supremely righteous-souled, and was pleased then.
Having accepted that maiden as a most beautiful wife, he lived glad in his own hermitage, free of fever.
[Bhishma said:] To one who has fallen into his own livelihood, whether wearing the mark or not, a gift should be given, they say, great king; both these are ascetics.
[Yudhishthira said:] What fault would there be, grandfather, in one who is purified by supreme faith and gives to a twice-born an offering to gods and ancestors, or a gift?
[Bhishma said:] A man purified by faith, dear one, though unrestrained, is without doubt purified everywhere; how much more you, lord of the earth.
[Yudhishthira said:] One should not examine a brahmana for rites to the gods; the wise say a brahmana is to be examined in giving to ancestors.
[Bhishma said:] A brahmana does not accomplish the offering; it succeeds through fate; sacrificers sacrifice by the grace of the gods; there is no doubt.
Brahmanas, best of the Bharatas, are always speakers of Brahman; the wise Markandeya said this long ago in these worlds.
[Yudhishthira said:] Whether unprecedented or learned, or a relative, or an ascetic or one given to sacrifice, how does he become a worthy vessel?
[Bhishma said:] Of good family, a doer of deeds, a physician, and non-cruel, modest, straight, truthful: these are worthy vessels, and the earlier three.
[Kashyapa said:] "All the Vedas with their six limbs, Sankhya, the Purana and birth in a good family are not a goal for a man devoid of conduct, king."
[Agni said:] "He who studies, thinking himself learned, and with knowledge destroys others' fame, Brahmana, does by that a killing of a Brahman; his worlds are perishable."
[Earth said:] "A thousand horse sacrifices and truth were weighed on a scale; I do not know whether half of this truth would be gained."
[Bhishma said:] Having so spoken, those four of boundless splendour quickly went: Earth, Kashyapa, Agni and Prakrishtayus Bhargava.
[Yudhishthira said:] These brahmanas in the world who keep vows eat the offering; how does what is eaten for a Brahman's sake become merit?
[Bhishma said:] Those brahmanas, king of kings, who are appointed and have crossed the Vedas, eat for Brahman's sake; they become those with broken vows.
[Yudhishthira said:] The wise say dharma is of many ways and not of one end; what is settled there? Tell me, grandfather.
[Bhishma said:] Non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, non-cruelty, self-control, and honesty, king of kings, are the settled marks of dharma.
Those who, praising dharma, wander this earth without practising that dharma, lord, delighting in mixture,
whoever gives them jewels, gold, cows or horses eats excrement for ten years, resorting to hell.
Of Medas, Pulkasas and Antavasayins, of those who babble of deeds done and not done from passion and delusion,
those fools who do not give the Vaishvadeva to a Brahmanical student, king of kings, enjoy unhappy worlds.
[Yudhishthira said:] What is the highest in celibacy, what the highest mark of dharma, and what is the best purity? Tell me, grandfather.
[Bhishma said:] Celibacy is highest, dear one, with avoidance of honey and meat; dharma stands in limit; peace is the mark of purity.
[Yudhishthira said:] At what time should one practise dharma, at what time pursue wealth, and at what time be happy? Tell me, grandfather.
[Bhishma said:] One should pursue wealth early, then dharma after, and afterward desire; and not go to attachment.
One should honour brahmanas and worship teachers, be agreeable to all beings, gentle in conduct and sweet in speech.
An untruth in office, tale-bearing to the king, and falsehood against the priest are equal to killing a brahmana.
One should not strike kings, nor kill a cow; whoever practises both is equal to killing an embryo.
One should never abandon the fire nor the Vedas, nor revile a brahmana; that is equal to killing a brahmana.
[Yudhishthira said:] What sort of brahmanas are good, and to whom is a gift of great fruit? To what sort should food be given? Tell me, grandfather.
[Bhishma said:] The angerless, devoted to dharma, ever true, delighting in self-control: such are good brahmanas, and a gift to them has great fruit.
The unproud, all-enduring, seers of purpose, masters of senses, friendly and kind to all beings: a gift to them has great fruit.
The ungreedy, pure, learned, modest, truthful, and those devoted to their own work: a gift to them has great fruit.
The best of the twice-born who studies the four Vedas with their limbs, turned back from the six actions, the sages know as the worthy vessel.
Those of this kind of qualities: a gift to them has great fruit; the giver to one worthy of the quality gains a thousandfold.
Endowed with wisdom, learning, conduct and character, a single best of the twice-born here could carry his whole family across.
One should give to such a one a cow, horse, wealth or grain, and other goods; he does not grieve after death.
Even one best of the twice-born could carry the whole family across; how much more more than one; therefore one should honour the worthy vessel.
If I am to hear it, king, tell me, best of kings; I shall remove your anger with every effort, lord of men.
I do not wish, best of men, for life nor the earth; I wish to do what is dear to you, king, scorcher of foes.
Hearing that the Vrishnis with the Bhojas, Kukuras and Andhakas had perished, the Pandavas, tormented with grief, were distressed in mind.
Shining with his own body, attended by divine weapons, the discus and others, by terrible divine persons in human form, waited upon by the hero Phalguna of fine splendour.
